english.title: Set a trap / snare to cause injury to a Schedule 6 or Schedule 6ZA wild animal - England
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) set in position in England a

(A)_[trap]_
(B)_[snare]_

of such a nature and so placed as to be calculated to cause bodily injury to a wild animal included in Schedule 6 or Schedule 6ZA to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 11(2)(b)(i) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 47 of the Agriculture (Wales) Act 2023 makes changes to the geographic region of this offence. This offence applies to England only. For the offence applying in Wales, see H101413. For the offence applying in England/Wales before the 17th October 2023, see H20031.(ii) See section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iii) See section 11(5) for presumption that animal is wild and section 27 for meaning of "wild animal".
(vi) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(vii) See Section 11(6) for defence.

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and / or a fine

Where more than one animal is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each animal (section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex, see section 20 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.
